comparison: Perfect agreement on probe design methodology (C69-C71). Both evaluations find the technical design principles well-supported. Peer reviewer notes improved clarity after revisions, while OpenEval confirms clear explanation with species-specific probe sets.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about C68 regarding co-expressed marker genes. OpenEval notes lack of experimental validation for functional claims, while peer reviewers suggest future studies to explore roles of co-expressed genes, indicating incomplete resolution.

Perfect agreement on speculative nature of mechanistic claims C85-C86. Both evaluations recognize these as hypotheses rather than demonstrated findings. OpenEval notes explicit speculation without direct mechanistic evidence; peer reviewers suggest future studies needed to establish these mechanisms.

Strong agreement on PdeI functional characterization (C45-C55). Both find convergence of structural, localization, and functional data convincing. Peer reviewers explicitly accept findings after initial concerns were addressed, noting the complex role of PdeI in c-di-GMP regulation.

Strong agreement on persister formation findings (C56-C64). Both evaluations accept the spatial localization and functional evidence linking PdeI to persister phenotype. OpenEval emphasizes integration of multiple data types; peer reviewers explicitly confirm acceptance of antibiotic killing and time-lapse imaging data.

Strong agreement on method efficiency and performance (C3, C10-C12, C19-C22). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative improvements across species; peer reviewers explicitly affirm high efficiency with over 90% mRNA detection for E. coli and describe method as straightforward and inexpensive. Peer review also includes cost analysis claims (C65, C87) and additional technical metrics (C32, C66-C67).

Agreement on robustness across bacterial species (C23-C31). OpenEval emphasizes consistency of performance metrics across diverse conditions; peer reviewers accept characterization results and acknowledge utility demonstrated for three model species. Peer review also addresses subpopulation detection (C33-C38) which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Agreement on biofilm heterogeneity and subpopulation identification. OpenEval addresses broader subpopulation detection (C33-C38) and biofilm-specific findings (C42-C44, C88-C89). Peer reviewers focus on biofilm base subpopulation (C39-C44, C89) and explicitly confirm convincing evidence for minority subpopulation detection.

Partial overlap on subpopulation identification across species (C33-C38). OpenEval groups these with biofilm-specific findings; peer reviewers evaluate them alongside general characterization data (C23-C31), confirming the method's ability to detect minority subpopulations in complex communities.

Partial overlap on biofilm reproducibility metrics (C39-C41). OpenEval evaluates these as quality control measures supporting method reliability; peer reviewers group them with biofilm heterogeneity findings and subpopulation detection, confirming reproducibility across replicates.

Agreement on cost-effectiveness claims (C65, C87). OpenEval finds quantitative cost comparison verifiable but notes potential overstatement of 'equipment-free' claim; peer reviewers describe method as 'straightforward and inexpensive,' supporting economic advantage without raising concerns about equipment claims.

Minor overlap on negative control data (C58). OpenEval evaluates BFP localization controls as supporting PdeI-specific findings; peer reviewers accept persister formation findings broadly without specifically addressing this control, though no concerns are raised about the localization data.

Minor overlap on prior work citation (C52). OpenEval notes this provides context for PdeI findings; peer reviewers accept the PdeI-c-di-GMP relationship after addressing initial concerns, implicitly accepting the contextual citations without specific comment.
